text:
Okay, so listen. You know how sometimes you drop your ice cream cone and nobody sees it? And you think, “Whew! Lucky me!” But then you feel all yucky inside because you know you *should* have said something? Well, my friend’s grown-ups are doing that, but with work stuff instead of sticky chocolate.

There’s this one guy, Mr. Henderson, who made a tiny mistake on the big computer thingy. Like, maybe he typed the wrong number or forgot a comma. It’s super small, so no one else noticed. Not even the boss lady! So now, another worker, Ms. Clara, is saying, “Just keep quiet! If we tell, they’ll get mad, and maybe we won’t get our bonus money.” That sounds scary, right? I’d be scared too.

But Mr. Henderson says, “No way. We have to say sorry.” He says if they hide it, the mistake might grow bigger later, like a monster under the bed. And that would be much worse. He thinks being honest makes them good people, even if they get in trouble now.

I don’t really understand why adults fight over such small things. Isn’t it better to just fix it? Like when I break my toy robot? My mom gets mad for five minutes, but then she helps me glue it back together, and it works again. If I hid the pieces, I’d never get my robot back. I hope they choose the fixing part. Hiding feels sneaky, and sneaking isn’t fun.
